about.note: Bank, cross-validation, final test opened, then the calling rule changed after it.

plan.title: Discover the data
plan.question: What does one row describe, which columns are there and what does each one mean, and what do a few rows look like?
plan.expected_output: The data card read with you: the row unit, the columns grouped with their meaning and availability, and a few example rows. Nothing is decided at this step.
plan.completion: Done once a first proposal is made.

plan.title: Define the prediction moment
plan.question: At what moment is the prediction made, and what is known at that moment?
plan.expected_output: A confirmed prediction time, restated and answered in your own words.

plan.title: Decide which variables are available at prediction time
plan.question: Which variables are known at the prediction moment, and which must be excluded?
plan.expected_output: A confirmed availability status for every candidate feature, with the exclusions listed in your own words.

plan.title: Split the data before exploring it
plan.question: How is the development set divided into folds for k-fold cross-validation, before any exploration of the target? Each fold is in turn the validation fold, predicted by a model fitted on the other folds, the training folds.
plan.expected_output: A confirmed cross-validation and a recorded fold assignment.
plan.completion: Decision split is confirmed and the split result is current.

plan.title: Fix the success criterion before seeing a model
plan.question: Precision is the share of the rows a rule selects that turn out positive; recall is the share of all positive rows the rule reaches. The baseline gives every row the same score, so its precision is the overall positive rate. The rule says which rows you act on: the top share or number of scores, or the rows above a score threshold. With a fixed number of rows acted on, precision, recall and lift rank the models the same way; with a threshold they differ. Choose the metric first. How many percentage points above the baseline, at the rule you will adopt, would make the model worth using? It is fixed now, before any model is fitted.
plan.expected_output: A confirmed metric and minimum gain over the baseline, stated before any model result is seen.

plan.title: Explore the development rows
plan.question: What do the development rows show about the outcome and the special values? Other explorations (the quality overview, rates by variable, distributions, the single-feature signal) each answer a question stated first; every look at the outcome is counted.
plan.expected_output: Target rate and special-value results on the development rows, with their exposure recorded.
plan.completion: The training EDA results are current.

plan.title: Decide how the model prepares the variables
plan.question: How should the model treat missing values, rare categories, extreme values and skewed variables? Every parameter is learnt only on the training folds of each model, never on its validation fold.
plan.expected_output: A confirmed preprocessing, with the explorations that motivated it.

plan.title: Fit a baseline and a logistic model
plan.question: How much does a simple model improve on a constant baseline, measured out of fold on the development rows?
plan.expected_output: Persisted out-of-fold predictions for the baseline and the logistic model.

plan.title: Choose the variants to compare
plan.question: Which variants of the candidate model, at most three and each with the question it answers, should be compared with it under the same evaluation: the penalty chosen by nested cross-validation, a stronger or weaker regularisation, the model without one group of variables, or another model family when the diagnostics show a pattern the linear model cannot follow?
plan.expected_output: A confirmed list of variants and their out-of-fold predictions, evaluated like the candidate.
plan.completion: Decision model_variant is confirmed and every variant fit is current.

plan.title: Choose a decision policy
plan.question: Which rule turns scores into actions (a threshold, a capacity or a share), and what does it cost and gain?
plan.expected_output: A current policy evaluation and a confirmed policy adoption.
plan.completion: The policy evaluation is current and decision policy is confirmed.

plan.title: Open the final test once
plan.question: Now that the model and the rule are chosen, do you open the sealed final test, once, to measure the chosen configuration on rows nothing has seen? After this, any change is made after the final test.
plan.expected_output: A confirmed opening in your own words, and the one evaluation of the chosen configuration on the final test.
plan.completion: Decision final_test is confirmed and the final evaluation is recorded.

plan.title: Conclude proportionately
plan.question: What can be said, for which use, and with which limits? Keeping the baseline is a valid result.
plan.expected_output: A confirmed conclusion that names its limits.

calibration.definition: The Brier score is the mean squared difference between the score and the outcome (0 or 1); the constant base rate gives the reference. A bin whose mean score lies outside the interval of its observed rate is miscalibrated.

coefficients.method: Wald intervals, estimate +- z * standard error, from the sandwich covariance H^-1 B H^-1 of the fit on every prepared row (H the penalised information, B the spread of the row scores): the delta-method approximation of a nonparametric bootstrap
coefficients.note: Coefficients of the model fitted on these rows, with Wald intervals from a robust (sandwich) standard error: the approximation of how much each coefficient would move if the rows were drawn again, the preparation of the variables kept as fitted. Associations given the other variables, never effects. The fit is penalised: its coefficients are pulled towards zero, so the intervals describe the spread of the penalised estimate, centred on a value that is itself shrunk; they are not exact confidence intervals of an unpenalised coefficient, and a coefficient of a rare category can be shrunk well inside its interval.
coefficients.scale: per standard deviation of the development rows (numeric) or per category (one-hot); associations, not effects

gain_points.definition: gain_points is the precision of the top share minus the base rate, in percentage points; recall is the share of the positive rows found (the cumulative gain).

values.counts: expected counts when a capacity cut splits a tie group (tied_at_cut)
values.note: The rule and the model are chosen on out-of-fold predictions of the development rows: these figures are development evidence, not independent evidence of future performance. No model was refitted.

selection.note: Under cross-validation each fold is scored by a model fitted on the other folds, so scores of different folds are not on the same scale (with temporal folds, each period is scored by a model of other periods). A capacity or a share is therefore applied within each fold: the best-scored share of each fold's rows, by that fold's model, and the counts are summed; by_fold gives each fold's precision. A threshold reads the scores as they are.

gain_points_variant.definition: gain_points is the precision of the top share minus the base rate, in percentage points; recall is the share of the positive rows found (the cumulative gain).

difference.definition: per-fold paired difference (this configuration minus the candidate), mean plus or minus one standard error

one_se.source: Hastie, Tibshirani & Friedman (2009), The Elements of Statistical Learning, 2nd ed., §7.10 (the one-standard-error rule)
one_se.text: The one-standard-error rule keeps the simplest configuration whose mean is within one standard error of the best one.

texts.en: The one-standard-error rule keeps the simplest configuration whose mean is within one standard error of the best one.
texts.fr: La règle d'une erreur type retient la configuration la plus simple dont la moyenne est à moins d'une erreur type de la meilleure.

one_se.simplicity: the linear family first, then fewer features, then a stronger penalty; a tie keeps the candidate

optimism.method: mean over folds of (the fold's best configuration minus the configuration best on the mean), in the direction of the metric
optimism.source: Tibshirani & Tibshirani (2009), A bias correction for the minimum error rate in cross-validation, Annals of Applied Statistics 3(2): 822-829
optimism.text: Choosing the best of several configurations on the same folds flatters it: the optimism is the average gap, fold by fold, between that fold's best configuration and the one chosen.

texts.en: Choosing the best of several configurations on the same folds flatters it: the optimism is the average gap, fold by fold, between that fold's best configuration and the one chosen.
texts.fr: Choisir la meilleure de plusieurs configurations sur les mêmes plis la flatte : l'optimisme est l'écart moyen, pli par pli, entre la meilleure configuration du pli et celle retenue.

optimism.note: Approximate: an estimate of how much the best mean owes to having chosen it among these configurations.

advice.text: The differences between the variants and the candidate stay within the noise between folds: another variant is unlikely to show a difference that chance would not explain. Stop here and choose.

The final test, opened once, is not affected by this choice.
